title: Casebook — projects from my sources
rules: Every fact comes from the linked article or the project's own website; nothing is added from memory.
Fields the sources don't give are marked 'Not stated' / 'Not named', or null for coordinates.
Projects are grouped by their main theme. 'themes' lists every theme that applies.

linkStatusKey.working: Loads and is free to read
linkStatusKey.broken: Doesn't load, or no longer shows the cited content. See 'replacement'.

projects.title: Murphy Crossing MARTA infill station
projects.location: Murphy Crossing, Southwest Atlanta, Georgia, USA (where Adair Park, West End and Oakland City meet), between MARTA's Oakland City and West End stations
projects.year: In study: five options revealed October 2026; preferred alternative due by summer 2027 at the latest
projects.designers: Atlanta Beltline Inc. (preliminary scoping study; principal engineer Shaun Green)
projects.scale: 20-acre Murphy Crossing site; 60-ft vertical gap between Beltline transit and MARTA rail; study costs about $800,000–$900,000

links.label: Atlanta Beltline — Murphy Crossing infill station virtual open house

projects.title: Atlanta Beltline Northwest Trail – Segment 2A
projects.location: Buckhead, Atlanta, Georgia, USA (from Bobby Jones Golf Course toward Peachtree Road; connects Collier Hills North and Colonial Homes)
projects.year: Groundbreaking October 2026; completion scheduled for early 2028
projects.designers: Heath & Lineback (designers); PATH Foundation (program manager); Hasbun Construction (contractor); Atlanta Beltline Inc.
projects.scale: 0.3-mile segment of 14-ft-wide multi-use trail, with a pedestrian bridge and an elevated trail structure; the full Northwest Trail will be 4.3 miles

projects.title: Federal Boulevard BRT
projects.location: Federal Boulevard, metro Denver, Colorado, USA
projects.year: Funding approved 23 October 2026; final design 2027; phase one (28 stations) starts fall 2027; phase two (46 stations) starts summer 2028
projects.designers: Not named by the source; funded by Colorado's Nonattainment Area Air Pollution Mitigation Enterprise
projects.scale: Up to 18 miles and 74 stations; $50 million plus $2.7 million a year for maintenance

projects.title: Oxford Street pedestrianisation
projects.location: Oxford Street, City of Westminster, London, UK (first phase: Orchard Street to Great Portland Street)
projects.year: First phase opened 26 October 2026; permanent scheme expected to start construction in 2027 and finish in 2028
projects.designers: East (lead) with Gehl, Publica, J&L Gibbons, Etude and NRP; Hawkins\Brown (long-term vision for the whole street); overseen by the Oxford Street Development Corporation (Mayor of London)
projects.scale: Almost 1 km traffic-free in the first phase, of a street about 2 km long; two new squares planned near Holles Street and Duke Street

projects.title: Jewel Streets Neighborhood Plan
projects.location: Jewel Streets, straddling East New York, Brooklyn and Lindenwood, Queens, New York City, USA
projects.year: Plan released October 2025; public review of rezoning and drainage plan expected to begin early 2028
projects.designers: NYC Department of Housing Preservation and Development (HPD) with the Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) and the Mayor's Office of Climate & Environmental Justice; community partners: Justice for the Jewel Streets Coalition (East New York Community Land Trust) and Cypress Hills Local Development Corporation
projects.scale: 12-block neighbourhood, including a 17-acre City-owned site; nearly $150 million in proposed infrastructure upgrades (per Urban Omnibus)
